subject: Packaging vs. Retain: Decision framework and revised price match offer
messages:
From: Emma Torres <emma@tidewave.io>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@tidewave.io, c.mendes@tidewave.io
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging decision next steps

Markus — thanks for the walkthrough this morning. We had an internal sync and want to push back on two items before we can move forward:

1) Total committed spend over 12 months — our renewal team is seeing a 20% delta versus our current vendor when we normalize for embeddings/epochs.
2) Migration assistance — engineering wants clarity on the runtime parity guarantees and a short replacement playbook if we need to roll back.

Can you share a simple side-by-side that shows pack-by-pack pricing (seats, reserved inference hours, embeddings blocks) and a pragmatic migration SLA?

Thanks,
Emma Torres
Director, Platform Partnerships
Tidewave Systems

Emma — appreciate the candid feedback. I’m looping in Vanessa (commercial) and Irene (solutions/ops) so we can give a concise, actionable reply. High level we can:

- Provide a line-item comparison that normalizes tokens, embedding units and reserved GPU-hour equivalents.
- Offer a limited pilot credit + migration support package (engineering time, runbook, rollback triggers).
- Match the effective per-token/embedding economics for the first 6 months with a targeted credit if we can agree on committed minimums.

We’ll push a formal breakdown by EOD tomorrow. Quick Q: is Tidewave comfortable with a 9–12 month committed term to bridge the gap, or does procurement need a 12-month firm?

Cheers,
Markus Klein

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Emma Torres <emma@tidewave.io>, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 08:53:00 -0700
Subject: Tidewave side-by-side: pricing & packaging (first pass)

Emma / team — thanks again. Attached is our first-pass side-by-side that maps Tidewave’s usage buckets to Redwood SKUs and shows an apples-to-apples effective rate. Highlights:

- Base match offer: for a 12-month commit of $750k ARR we can apply an up-front credit that brings your effective per-embedding unit to within 3% of your current vendor for the first 6 months.
- Pilot credits: $60k in engineering credits for migration validation and two onsite/remote handoffs.
- Rollback SLA: we commit to a documented rollback playbook and a 48-hour critical-path escalation path to revert to a retained variant if severe regressions occur.

Open items for procurement: whether Tidewave needs seat licenses or pure consumption billing; and tax/PO constraints that affect timing.

Irene — can you confirm the rollback playbook items (KV cache snapshot cadence, fallback model variant, and egress handling) and whether the 48-hour SLA is operationally feasible?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_packaging_options_v2.pdf (updated)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, Emma Torres <emma@tidewave.io>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Tidewave side-by-side: pricing & packaging (first pass)

Emma / team — quick ops confirmation. 48-hour rollback SLA is aggressive but achievable if we pre-agree on:

- A locked initial model variant and a rehearse window (7 days) during pilot to validate quality gates.
- Daily KV-cache snapshots and prefix cache export at t=0 and after pilot validation.
- A standby dedicated capacity pool that can be re-attached to the prior model variant within 12–24 hours for a full rollback (customer pays for standby only if exercised).
- Cutover checklist and a defined metric regression threshold (BLEU/ROUGE surrogate or human-sampled anomaly rate) to trigger rollback.

I’ll attach the operational checklist and a concise migration runbook draft.

Irene Choi
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@tidewave.io>

Team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Procurement wants two clarifications before we take this to legal:

1) The credit structure: is the 6-month effective match delivered as an up-front credit or as monthly bill-back? We prefer monthly bill-back to smooth cash flow.
2) Standby capacity costs: Tidewave can agree to standby during the 3-month migration window but needs a cap on accidental standby charges if we exceed the expected validation period.

Technical note from eng: we need a short runbook excerpt that shows how you guarantee identical tokenization/embedding parity — mismatches there are our main concern.

Regards,
Carlos Mendes
Head of Cloud Architecture, Tidewave Systems

Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tidewave side-by-side: pricing & packaging (first pass)

Carlos / Emma — quick answers and the proposed contract language we’ll send to Legal (draft attached):

1) Credit structure: we can structure the 6-month economic match as monthly bill-back credits applied as invoice adjustments. That aligns with Tidewave’s cashflow ask. We’ll include an explicit schedule of adjustments in the SOW.

2) Standby cap: we propose a staircase cap — $8k/day for the first 14 days of standby, then $4k/day thereafter up to a 90-day max during the migration period. If we need to extend beyond the 90 days because of unforeseen infra issues, standby continues at the $4k/day rate with a 30-day notice and mutual sign-off.

3) Tokenization/embeddings parity: our engineering team will provide a short technical appendix demonstrating deterministic tokenizer settings, embedding vector similarity thresholds, and a small reference dataset run. That appendix will be part of the SOW and validated during pilot.

Next steps: I’ll upload the redlined SOW with the monthly credit schedule and standby cap and request a procurement call early next week to align PO timing. If procurement is comfortable with the staircase cap, we can lock commercial terms and move to legal.

Thanks — appreciate the constructive back-and-forth.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
